---
title: "Empirical reproducibility"
subtitle: "Survey statistics reproduced from the original 103 × 32 CSV"
---

This report is regenerated from the anonymous response matrix. Reproduced values are distinguishable from source-reported SPSS targets, and all code is available in the repository. Data are cross-sectional five-point Likert responses from a selected sample of finance professionals, not a country panel.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("analysis/master.R")
source("R/functions.R")
read_table <- function(name) {
  utils::read.csv(file.path("outputs/tables", name), check.names = FALSE)
}
```

## Data and measurement

Composite scores use the unweighted **mean of each construct's stated items**. The codebook maps original V1–V32 codes to the SPSS construct abbreviations. The source file contains no missing item responses.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-validation
#| tbl-cap: "Input validation: counts and checks"
knitr::kable(read_table("input_validation.csv"), digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive
#| tbl-cap: "Construct-level descriptive statistics"
knitr::kable(read_table("construct_descriptives.csv"), digits = 3)
```

## Internal consistency

Cronbach's alpha is calculated from item covariance/total-score variance, using raw unstandardized item responses. Alpha is a measure of internal consistency, not proof of validity or dimensionality.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reliability
#| tbl-cap: "Five construct scales: Cronbach alpha"
knitr::kable(read_table("reliability.csv"), digits = 3)
```

## Bivariate associations

Pearson correlations below describe sample associations between four independently defined composite predictors and the dependent composite *CFA*. Reported p-values assume the usual independent-observation sampling model; they should not be read as representative-population or causal evidence.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-correlations
#| tbl-cap: "Pearson r against perceived architecture effectiveness"
knitr::kable(read_table("pearson_correlations.csv"), digits = 3)
```

## Multiple regression

The fitted *associational* model is

$$
\mathrm{CFA}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1\mathrm{IC}_i + \beta_2\mathrm{BFD}_i +
\beta_3\mathrm{PRA}_i + \beta_4\mathrm{TAFU}_i + u_i.
$$

Standardized coefficients are the unstandardized slopes multiplied by $s_{X_j}/s_Y$, so that values can be compared directly with S2's standardized coefficients. Intercept is not standardized.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ols
#| tbl-cap: "OLS slopes, conventional confidence intervals, and standardized coefficients"
knitr::kable(read_table("ols_coefficients.csv"), digits = 4)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model
#| tbl-cap: "OLS model summary"
knitr::kable(read_table("model_summary.csv"), digits = 4)
```

## Source-reported SPSS comparison

The results above are computed from the raw CSV. The independent R tests compare them with the rounded coefficients in S2 (recorded in `data/reference/spss_published_benchmarks.csv`). Neither the supplemental rounded results nor the private `.spv` are used as *inputs* to calculate the R estimates.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spss
#| tbl-cap: "Reference values as reported in the supplied supplementary material"
bench <- utils::read.csv("data/reference/spss_published_benchmarks.csv")
knitr::kable(bench[bench$metric %in% c("pearson_r", "standardized_beta",
  "model_r_squared", "model_adjusted_r_squared"),
  c("metric", "construct_or_variable", "reported_value")], digits = 3)
```

## Diagnostics and sensitivity

The code exports variance inflation factors, influence-count summaries, and a leave-one-observation-out range for each slope. Individual-row influence diagnostics are stored locally and ignored by Git. These are *diagnostics*, not grounds to delete a respondent without a pre-specified rule.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-vif
#| tbl-cap: "Variance inflation factors"
knitr::kable(read_table("vif.csv"), digits = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Leave-one-respondent-out OLS sensitivity (unstandardized slopes)"
knitr::kable(read_table("leave_one_out_summary.csv"), digits = 4)
```

If the optional R package `sandwich` is installed, `analysis/02_reproduce.R` also writes an **exploratory HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust** table; it is intentionally not presented as the original SPSS analysis or evidence of causal effects.
